description: The complete Node-only agent backend under src/agent/**, built in the spec's section-7 security-first order: workspace boundary (FileAccess + ignore rules) with node:test coverage, read tools, WS protocol types, pairing HTTP+WS server, prompt-driven AIProvider loop with 8-round cap, suggest-only propose_patch, device-side runtime-log tool executors, per-question run-report append, and the cli.ts + src/ai/index-agent.js bin wrapper + packaging. This feature is self-contained: it never imports RN code and leaves a buildable, testable agent binary. Depends on nothing. (The device client that answers the runtime-log tool_calls is FEAT-002; until then the log tools are exercised by the smoke client in step verification.)
steps: Add optional `aiAgentURL?: string` to AppLensConfig in src/core/AppLensConfig.ts (JSDoc: undefined = agent feature off) and add `aiAgentURL: undefined` to DEFAULT_CONFIG.

Create src/agent/workspace/FileAccess.ts: realpath(root) up front; resolve(relativePath) rejects absolute inputs and `..` escapes, path.resolve against the real root, then realpath the target and re-check it is still inside the real root (defeats symlink escape); readFile(path, range?) enforces a 100 KB size cap and a binary sniff (reject NUL / non-UTF-8). Pure Node, no ws/model imports. Follow the FileAccess sample in docs/AGENT_MODE_PROPOSAL.md.
Create src/agent/workspace/ignoreRules.ts: deny-list node_modules, .git, .env*, *.pem, *.keystore, *.jks, id_rsa*; honor .gitignore where cheap. Consumed by FileAccess and the read tools.

Create src/agent/workspace/FileAccess.test.ts using node:test + node:assert. Set up a temp workspace with fixtures including a symlink pointing outside the root. Cover: ../ escape rejected, absolute path rejected, symlink-escape rejected, in-workspace read ok, deny-list enforced, size cap enforced. Add root package.json script "test:agent": "node --test dist/agent/workspace/".

Create the read tools: src/agent/tools/listFiles.ts (listFiles(dir?) → depth-limited, ignore-filtered tree), src/agent/tools/searchCode.ts (searchCode(query, glob?) → Node fs walk + regex returning file+line+context, no external rg), src/agent/tools/readFile.ts (readFile(path, range?) delegating to FileAccess.readFile). All paths validated through FileAccess.

Create src/agent/protocol.ts exporting the WS message TYPES exactly as spec section 2: ask {type,id,question,conversation:AIMessage[]}; agent→device token {type,askId,delta}, patch {type,askId,path,diff,rationale}, answer {type,askId,text,usage:AIUsage}, error {type,askId,message}; device-side tool_call {type,callId,name:'get_network_logs'|'get_console_logs',args}, tool_result {type,callId,result}; plus the POST /pair request/response shapes {clientInfo} -> {token,wsUrl}. These TYPES are the only src/agent surface later re-exported from the barrel (FEAT-002).

Add `ws` to package.json dependencies pinned to a current stable release. Create src/agent/server.ts: HTTP server with POST /pair that mints a short-lived single-session token and returns {token,wsUrl}; WS upgrade validates the token (query param/subprotocol) and rejects anything else; bind 127.0.0.1 by default; one session = one loop instance bound to the paired socket.

Create src/agent/tools/runtimeLogTools.ts: agent-side executors for get_network_logs/get_console_logs that send a tool_call over the WS and await the matching tool_result (correlated by callId) with a count cap and a timeout. (The device answers these in FEAT-002.)

Create src/agent/loop/agentLoop.ts: wrap createAIProvider(config)/chatStream; a system prompt that describes the six tools and a STRICT JSON tool-call format; parse tool-call JSON from the model, dispatch to local file tools or device-side log tools, feed results back, repeat; stream reply tokens out as token messages; emit a patch message when the model calls propose_patch; hard cap of 8 tool rounds.

Create src/agent/tools/proposePatch.ts: input target path + proposed new content (or diff); output a unified diff string + short rationale; WRITES NOTHING; validate the target path through FileAccess so a patch cannot name a file outside the workspace.

Add the per-question run-report append: on each answered question, append to applens-agent-report.md in the TARGET project root (question, tools called with args, files read, proposed diffs, final answer + confidence). This is the ONLY allowed write and is the agent's own report, never project source. Implement in agentLoop.ts or a small src/agent/loop/reportWriter.ts.

Create src/agent/cli.ts: parse --project (default cwd), --port, --host (default 127.0.0.1; 0.0.0.0 only with the explicit flag plus a printed LAN-exposure warning), --token (optional). Resolve + validate the project root up front; print workspace + loopback URL + pairing token; start server.ts.

Create src/ai/index-agent.js mirroring src/ai/index-project-ast.js: require the compiled ../agent/cli from dist with a ts-node transpileOnly fallback and clear usage/error messages. Add "applens-agent": "dist/ai/index-agent.js" to package.json bin.
Confirm tsconfig.build.json compiles src/agent/** with no config change (its include is already src/**).
acceptance_criteria: npm run type-check passes with the new config field and all src/agent/** modules present.
npm run build emits dist/agent/cli.js, dist/ai/index-agent.js, and dist/agent/workspace/FileAccess.js.
npm run build && npm run test:agent passes all six FileAccess cases: ../ escape rejected, absolute rejected, symlink-escape rejected, in-workspace read ok, deny-list enforced, size cap enforced.
propose_patch writes nothing to project source; the only file the agent writes is applens-agent-report.md in the target project root.
The server binds 127.0.0.1 by default; POST /pair returns {token,wsUrl}; a WS upgrade with a bad/missing token is rejected.
No file under src/agent/** imports from src/agent-client/** or any RN/.tsx module.
verification: Manual: start `node dist/ai/index-agent.js --project .` (or npx applens-agent --project .), confirm it prints the workspace, a 127.0.0.1 listen URL and a token; POST /pair returns a token+wsUrl; a WS upgrade with a wrong token is refused.
findings:
FEAT-002 (device client / AITab wiring) will consume the following from this feature:

--- Protocol TYPES (src/agent/protocol.ts — RN-safe, no Node imports; re-export ONLY these from src/index.ts) ---
Exported interfaces/types: AskMessage, TokenMessage, PatchMessage, AnswerMessage, ErrorMessage, ToolCallMessage, ToolResultMessage, DeviceToAgentMessage (= AskMessage | ToolResultMessage), AgentToDeviceMessage (= Token|Patch|Answer|Error|ToolCall), AgentMessage (union of both directions), DeviceToolName (= 'get_network_logs' | 'get_console_logs'), NetworkLogSummary, ConsoleLogSummary, PairRequest, PairResponse.
Message shapes (exact field names):
  ask         { type:'ask', id, question, conversation: AIMessage[] }
  token       { type:'token', askId, delta }
  patch       { type:'patch', askId, path, diff, rationale }
  answer      { type:'answer', askId, text, usage: AIUsage }
  error       { type:'error', askId, message }
  tool_call   { type:'tool_call', callId, name: DeviceToolName, args: Record<string,unknown> }
  tool_result { type:'tool_result', callId, result: unknown }
The device correlates its streamed reply by `askId` (== the ask's `id`) and answers each tool_call by echoing its `callId`.

--- Pairing / token scheme ---
HTTP: POST /pair with JSON body { clientInfo?: Record<string,unknown> } (body is advisory in M1, drained+ignored) -> 200 JSON PairResponse { token, wsUrl }. The token is a 48-hex-char single-session secret (crypto.randomBytes(24)). Default port 4747; wsUrl is `ws://<host>:<port>/?token=<token>` (host 0.0.0.0 is rewritten to 127.0.0.1 in the printed URL). WS upgrade requires the token as the `?token=` QUERY PARAM; a missing/wrong token is rejected with a raw `HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized`. A minted token expires after 5 min if unused and is re-minted on each /pair; a fixed --token never expires. The device must therefore POST /pair, then open the returned wsUrl verbatim.

--- Device-side tool_result shapes the AgentClient must return ---
get_network_logs -> NetworkLogSummary[]  = { method, url, status?, durationMs?, timestamp }[]  (map from AppLensStorage.getNetworkRequests(): NetworkRequest -> {method,url,status,duration->durationMs,timestamp}).
get_console_logs -> ConsoleLogSummary[]  = { level, message, timestamp }[]  (map from AppLensStorage.getLogs(): LogEntry -> {level,message,timestamp}).
Both tool_call args carry { count: number } (agent caps count to [1,200], default 50); the device should return at most `count` entries (newest-most-relevant) to avoid overflowing a WS frame. Values are already redacted at capture. Agent-side timeout for a tool_result is 15s (DEFAULT_TOOL_TIMEOUT_MS / TOOL_TIMEOUT_MS); the device should answer promptly.

--- Report file ---
The agent appends to `applens-agent-report.md` in the TARGET PROJECT ROOT (constant REPORT_FILE in src/agent/loop/reportWriter.ts). It is the agent's own audit log and the ONLY file the agent writes — it is NOT project source and should be gitignored, never committed. propose_patch writes nothing.

--- Other integration facts ---
- Config: AppLensConfig.aiAgentURL?: string added (undefined = agent off); DEFAULT_CONFIG.aiAgentURL = undefined. AITab probes this on mount per the plan's addressing rules (iOS sim 127.0.0.1, Android emu 10.0.2.2, physical device LAN IP + --host 0.0.0.0).
- Bin: `applens-agent` -> dist/ai/index-agent.js (ts-node transpileOnly fallback). CLI flags: --project (default cwd), --port (4747), --host (127.0.0.1; 0.0.0.0 prints a LAN warning), --token.
- The agent loop is prompt-driven JSON tool-calls (model replies with {"tool":"<name>","args":{...}} or final prose ending 'Confidence: High|Medium|Low'); 8-round cap (MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS). Six tools: list_files, search_code, read_file (local via FileAccess) + get_network_logs, get_console_logs (device via DeviceBridge) + propose_patch (suggest-only diff).
- AIProvider backend for the agent comes from DEFAULT_CONFIG overridden by env vars APPLENS_AI_PROVIDER / APPLENS_AI_API_KEY / APPLENS_AI_MODEL / APPLENS_AI_BASE_URL (the agent never imports RN AppLens core).
- Deps: `ws` ^8.18.0 in dependencies, `@types/ws` ^8.5.10 in devDependencies.

Verification run: npm run type-check (clean), npm run build (emits dist/agent/cli.js, dist/ai/index-agent.js, dist/agent/workspace/FileAccess.js; no src/agent leak into dist/index.js|.d.ts), npm run test:agent (6/6 FileAccess cases pass), and the manual server start (POST /pair -> {token,wsUrl}; WS good token accepted, wrong token -> HTTP 401).
